effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % reduction in HC at plot and stream scales; greatest reductions: -1.32% at KS31 plot, -0.14% and -0.17% in streams of K2 and K3
design_spec_detail: Six check-dams in main streams; sedimentation area per dam: 3 m2 (1 m width x 3 m length, parallel to stream); C-RUSLE value 0.001 for sedimentation area; located where HC above 90th percentile, close to trails, separated along streams
context_conditions: Steep hillslopes with narrow valley bottoms; small sedimentation area (0.005-0.007% of total subcatchment area); effectiveness described as satisfactory given small area affected
evidence_quote: recommend construction of check-dams as somewhat effective landscape features to reduce hydrological connectivity and thus sediment and radionuclide delivery

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: slight reduction in HC across all compartments; reductions between 1.5% and 3.1% in plantation areas one year after FMO
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Progressive understory vegetation recovery after tree thinning; understory canopy cover remained lower than pre-FMO; HC remained higher than pre-FMO throughout recovery period
evidence_quote: progressive vegetation recovery after the FMO triggered a slight reduction of connectivity in all compartments of both subcatchments

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Check dams reduced simulated hydrological connectivity but did not prevent the general increasing trend post-fire
design_spec_detail: 23 check dams (12 wooden, 11 concrete) built in main streams; modelled as non-silted, partially silted, and completely silted stages
context_conditions: Effective only at short distance and short term; most dams nearly silted after one rain event (60 mm in 6 h, 3 months post-fire); fully silted after 2.5 years
evidence_quote: Check dams reduced connectivity but did not prevent the general trend.
locator: Abstract; Results: Evolution of Hydrological Connectivity; Further Research and Suggested Practices

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Vegetation recovery scenarios (10%, 15%, 25%, 75%) progressively reduced simulated HC; 75% recovery yielded HC below pre-fire levels in most sub-catchments
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Effectiveness greater than check dams once sufficient cover achieved; homogeneous recovery assumed in model; actual patchy recovery recommended
evidence_quote: effectiveness of the small and future vegetation recovery reducing the values of HC was greater than the role played by the partially and silted check dams
locator: Results: Evolution of Hydrological Connectivity; Conclusions (ii)

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Recommended for hillslopes disturbed by salvage logging, not just channel check dams
evidence_quote: it is necessary to carry out some post-fire erosion management in hillslopes

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: not reported
evidence_quote: simple changes in road design that would reduce drainage concentration could minimize road-related adverse impact

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Cross-banks highly effective for coarse sediment but ineffective for fine-grained fractions at the bank
design_spec_detail: Cross-banks 5-6 m wide, ~0.5 m high, placed at regular intervals along snig track (15 m standard interbank length in experiments); spacing varies by soil type and slope per EPA 1998
context_conditions: Effective for coarse sediment trapping; fine sediment bypasses cross-bank in overland flow; effectiveness varies with rainfall intensity, time since logging, and soil type
evidence_quote: cross-banks were highly effective in controlling coarse sediment movement by trapping such material in the channel formed by the cross-bank

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % of predicted mean plume lengths exceeding available hillslope length (0.5–16% depending on rainfall intensity and age); volume of overland flow reaching stream predicted probabilistically
design_spec_detail: Generic equations derived for trade-off between intercross-bank length (L) and flow path distance (H) to stream; design criterion: LV15/3μvbt5 + f·LV15·√(σvbt5²)/3μvbt5² ≤ H; f=1.645 for 95% non-exceedance; Figure 11 provides design chart for three runoff rates
context_conditions: Works better with longer available hillslope dispersal length; less effective on steep, dissected terrain (metasediment) where tracks are closer to streams; effectiveness declines with high rainfall intensity and recently logged sites (<1.5 years)
evidence_quote: Generic equations guiding the trade-off between intercross-bank length and flow path distance from cross-bank outlet to stream needed for infiltration

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % average reduction in sediment load at water bar outlet across all sites
design_spec_detail: Water bars constructed every 20–30 m along skid tracks according to soil type and slope; dimensions 5–6 m wide, 0.5 m high average
context_conditions: Effective for coarse sediment; markedly less effective for fine <63 µm material; effectiveness varies by soil type, rainfall intensity, and time since disturbance (0.5–5 years)
evidence_quote: on average, there was a 60% reduction in sediment load as runoff was diverted at the outlet of the bar across all sites

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: runoff from water bar failed to reach plot boundary during majority of low- to medium-intensity events on older sites; 43% of remobilised sediment retained in GHA over 6 years
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: GHA acts as high-infiltration vegetative filter downslope of water bars; more effective on older (5-year) sites; fine-grained material more likely to pass through
evidence_quote: The GHA is clearly operating as a vegetative filter...effectively reduces sediment fluxes as runoff is delivered from key source areas

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Filter strip retained ~8 times more 137Cs per unit area than GHA; 28% of total skid track losses retained in filter strip over 6 years
design_spec_detail: Stream-side filter strips retained on all streams, width 20–30 m; vehicle entry and ground disturbance prohibited
context_conditions: Per unit area most effective buffer; receives fine-grained material propagating through GHA or directly from water bars; risk of over-reliance on filter strips if GHA performance is poor
evidence_quote: the filter strip retained ø times the 137Cs and associated sediment of the GHA

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Suggested as improvement to reduce volume of overland flow discharging onto any one point on GHA
evidence_quote: decreasing the spacing of water bars on skid tracks thus reducing the volume of overland flow discharging onto any one point on the GHA

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % of fine-grained material deposited on hillslope over 55 m flow path; 50–85% of eroded snig track material stored at cross-bank
design_spec_detail: Cross-banks 5–6 m wide, 0.5 m high on average, placed at regular intervals according to soil type and slope; designed to pond then redirect runoff and sediment onto adjacent GHA
context_conditions: Effectiveness dependent on percentage fine fraction in eroded sediment, slope at base of cross-bank, and timing/frequency of large rainfall events post-logging; bank overtopping observed on granite sites within 3–4 years after logging
evidence_quote: Over 50% of fine-grained material were deposited on the hillslope over a relatively short, flow path length of 55 m
locator: Abstract; Study Area; Results - Sediment delivery and storage; Discussion

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % deposition of silt and clay fraction over 55 m flow path through GHA
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Rough, sparsely vegetated GHA surface reduces flow velocities and promotes deposition; less effective under extreme rainfall intensities where continuous flow paths develop; fine fraction enriched in sorbed pollutants may still be delivered
evidence_quote: deposition of, on average, 65±26% of the silt and clay fraction [over GHA flow path]
locator: Results - Sediment delivery and storage; Discussion

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % of clearcut/site-prepared area not contributing to SMZ breakthroughs
design_spec_detail: SMZ widths at least 20 or 40 ft for intermittent/perennial streams on slight slopes (<20%), 35 or 70 ft on moderate slopes (21-40%) per Georgia BMP guidelines; observed mean SMZ width 75 ft
context_conditions: Effective for 95% of area but fails in convergent topography, large contributing areas, steep slopes, high bare ground, and road/skid trail drainage points
evidence_quote: SMZ widths are adequate for runoff originating from 95 percent of recent clearcut and site-prepared areas.

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Recommended for areas with large contributing area and steep slopes; dispersal of road runoff before it concentrates
evidence_quote: reduction of bare ground, better dispersal of road runoff, introduction of hydraulic resistance to likely flow paths

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: Variable SMZ width based on contributing area, slope, and litter cover; extended in sensitive/convergent areas, possibly shortened elsewhere; secondary SMZ zone where ground disturbance prohibited
context_conditions: Recommended where breakthroughs likely: larger contributing area, steeper slopes, less litter cover
evidence_quote: SMZ widths should be variable and based on physical features of the site... extended in sensitive areas where breakthroughs are likely.

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: Maintain organic litter cover on soils during forest operations across silvicultural sites and especially in variable source areas near SMZ
context_conditions: Bare ground and low litter cover key predictors of breakthroughs; maintaining litter reduces runoff and erosion
evidence_quote: results reinforce the importance of maintaining organic litter cover on soils during forest operations to minimize runoff and erosion

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: Stacking of logging slash along SMZ boundaries and in old agricultural gullies
context_conditions: Recommended as simple remedy especially in gullies draining >0.1 acre which frequently contribute to breakthroughs
evidence_quote: stacking of logging slash along SMZ boundaries and in old agricultural gullies... BMP efficiency can be greatly improved

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % reduction in mean IC (sediment connectivity index) from 0 to 90 basins; optimal scenario (30 basins) identified via mean change point method
design_spec_detail: Optimal number: 30 sediment basins placed at road drainage outlets on segments with upslope drainage area ≥2 ha; maximum possible 90 basins in 6.4 km² watershed
context_conditions: Diminishing returns beyond 30 basins (upslope area <1.99 ha); applicable to this watershed and topographically similar mountainous watersheds; assumed 100% sediment retention efficiency in model
evidence_quote: optimal number of sediment basins is 30 and the corresponding road segments' upslope drainage areas were 2 ha

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: maximum reduction in mean IC value (buffer_160 vs no buffer); optimal width (64 m) identified via mean change point method; IC reduction range 0.020–0.121 across widths 32–160 m
design_spec_detail: Optimal riparian buffer width: 64 m along streams; tree-dominated vegetation assumed; sediment retention efficiency at 64 m = 35.3% (Y=39.56×(1−exp(−0.035×x)))
context_conditions: Diminishing returns beyond 64 m width; effectiveness depends on soil type, slope, vegetation, topography; sediment basins prioritised over riparian buffers as more effective; buffers 64–96 m may overlap road zones causing local IC increase
evidence_quote: optimal width of riparian buffers is 64 m… sediment connectivity decreased sharply when riparian buffer widths were in the 0–64 m zones

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Mg sediment trapped in four basins after three post-fire storms (observed); model predicted 139.6 Mg
design_spec_detail: Four sediment basins installed below culverts on Road 2; sub-catchment areas 0.9, 1.05, 1.38, 4.1 ha; open/weir-type outlet; basins located on lower slopes near fire perimeter boundary
context_conditions: Post-wildfire condition; gravelled crowned road (Road 2) at 7% gradient with upslope ditches and culverts routing flow to basins; high-severity burn upslope
evidence_quote: Eldorado County had to empty four sediment basins beside Road 2, removing an estimated 134 m3 (about 120 Mg)
locator: Section 2.2 (study site), Section 3.5 (comparison of modelling to observed), Section 4.7 (road design)

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Road 2 ditch and culverts prevented upslope runoff from flooding over road and eroding slopes below; sub-catchments below Road 2 showed net deposition
design_spec_detail: Road 2: gravelled, crowned, insloped with upslope armoured ditches and regularly spaced culverts draining to sediment basins; road gradient ~7%
context_conditions: Post-wildfire; insloped crowned road design with upslope drain intercepts hillslope runoff before it overtops road surface; effective where road gradient allows ditch and culvert system to function
evidence_quote: upslope armoured ditches and regularly spaced culverts on road 2 demonstrate the potential for road networks to reduce erosion risks

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Road 1 (outsloped, no ditches/culverts) did not intercept upstream flow paths; flow continued over road surface depositing sediment but maintaining connectivity downslope
design_spec_detail: Road 1: paved, flat/outsloped, no upslope drain or culverts within eastern burn area; gradient ~4%
context_conditions: Road 1 outsloped without drainage infrastructure allowed flow paths to pass over road, depositing sediment on road surface but not disconnecting hillslope from downslope areas; contrast with Road 2 insloped design
evidence_quote: Road 1 is relatively flat and lacking culverts or an inside drainage ditch...much of the upslope runoff either followed or crossed over the road surface

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % reduction in sediment delivery from mulching at 1–2 Mg/ha compared to untreated (ERMiT model predictions, Table 8)
design_spec_detail: Mulching at 1 Mg/ha and 2 Mg/ha application rates modelled on 60-m hillslope, 30.7% slope, moderate severity fire
context_conditions: Post-wildfire hillslope treatment; modelled only—no opportunity to install before storms; effectiveness varies by storm return period
evidence_quote: mulching reduces the estimated sediment delivery about 50%, and contoured logs by 10–12 Mg/ha depending on log diameter and spacing
locator: Section 4.9 (estimated impacts of erosion mitigation); Table 8

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Reduction of 10–12 Mg/ha in sediment delivery depending on log diameter and spacing (ERMiT model, Table 8)
design_spec_detail: Log erosion barriers (contour logs): 0.15 m diameter at 20 m spacing and 0.15 m diameter at 10 m spacing; modelled on 60-m hillslope, 30.7% slope, moderate severity post-fire
context_conditions: Post-wildfire hillslope treatment; modelled only—not installed before observed storms; 10 m spacing more effective than 20 m spacing
evidence_quote: Log erosion barriers, 0.15 m dia, 20 m spacing...0.15 m dia, 10 m spacing [reduce sediment delivery 10–12 Mg/ha]
locator: Section 4.9 (estimated impacts of erosion mitigation); Table 8

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % reduction in simulated basin-wide HOF if all roads recover to abandoned skid trail condition

evidence_quote: simulated basin-wide HOF from all roads/trails declined by almost 50% from 5326 to 2729 m3

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: Minimizing road/trail density; avoiding excessive excavation on midslope sites; minimizing steep skid trails draining into forest roads; avoiding wet/unstable sites; limiting depth of excavation; minimizing road length and connectivity
context_conditions: Most effective where subsurface flow interception and intense rainfall are significant; road removal considered not cost-justifiable for high-density networks in SE Asia
evidence_quote: most cost-effective means to avoid adverse hydrological changes...minimizing road/trail density, avoiding excessive excavation on midslope sites
locator: Discussion, Impact reduction section; Abstract; Conclusion

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Road removal involving hillslope re-contouring discussed but deemed not cost-justifiable for high-density logging networks in SE Asia; evidence of restoring hillslope flow pathways lacking
evidence_quote: Road removal...has been applied elsewhere...costs associated with these types of activity are probably not justifiable for most logging sites in SE Asia

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: SST hazard remains medium to high despite measures; longitudinal connectivity disrupted
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Check dams, bricked steps, bank fortification applied in Huciva Desna; SST hazard still medium-high; hungry water effect observed below check dams
evidence_quote: Despite the installment of technical measures such as check dams, series of bricked steps, bank fortification...degree of SST hazard is still medium to high.

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: roads along channels described as decreasing slope-channel connectivity, functioning as buffers
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Paved parallel roads along channels in Upper Moravice and Huciva Desna watersheds act as buffers reducing lateral sediment connectivity
evidence_quote: All three applied methods confirmed that the parallel roads along channels decrease slope-channel connectivity, especially in the Upper Moravice catchment.

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: check dams reduce bedload transport downstream and decrease longitudinal connectivity but cause hungry water effect
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Check dams in Huciva Desna (density 5 per km); incision observed below check dams; hungry water effect documented
evidence_quote: Check dams primarily stabilize riverbeds, reduce bedload transport downstream...decrease longitudinal sediment connectivity...incision caused by 'hungry water effects' downstream.

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % of river length with reduced sediment supply from banks
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Bank fortification (bricked walls and rip-raps) reduces lateral sediment supply; 30% of Huciva Desna length modified; 1% of Upper Moravice length modified
evidence_quote: The sediment supply from river banks of Upper Moravice is decreased by 10% and Huciva Desna by 33% of its total length by bank fortification.

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: check-dam efficiency contested; considered short-term solution with high economic cost and downstream erosion effects
design_spec_detail: Height 6.25–6.45 m, width 36–38.75 m, sediment trap efficiency 30.9–55.3%; constructed 2013 post-fire
context_conditions: Post-fire Mediterranean semi-arid headwater catchments; silting occurs in first years after fire
evidence_quote: efficiency of this measure has been widely contested for being a short-term solution with high economic cost

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: fire-affected steep terrain, Mediterranean; cited as quick low-cost alternative to check-dams
evidence_quote: Easy-Barriers on steep terrains affected by fires as a quick, low-cost solution to decrease the peak flow

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: log erosion barriers and contour-felled log debris proved efficient to retain sediments and limit nutrient losses
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: post-fire hillslope stabilisation in Mediterranean forest; also supported vegetation recovery
evidence_quote: log erosion barriers and contour-felled log debris, which were proved efficient to retain sediments and limit nutrient losses

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: SCSTREAM maps recommended to identify optimal hillslope placement of sediment control measures
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Mediterranean fire-affected catchments with intense rainfall events driving effective sediment transport
evidence_quote: SCSTREAM maps to place sediment control measures at hillslopes for intense rainfall events when effective sediment transport happens

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Upland forested watersheds; measure inferred from finding that larger road-stream distances associate with better geomorphic condition
evidence_quote: minimizing roads in close proximity to waterways…basis of successful watershed restoration programs to mitigate the impacts of roads

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Proportion of road length delivering sediment dropped from 14–61% (baseline) to 4–29% (current) with engineered drains; sediment delivered dropped from 6–38% to 2–21%
design_spec_detail: Minimum drain spacing of 30 m applied; engineered drains include relief culverts, water-bars, and rolling dips; optimization places new drains at 1-m increments along segments, prioritising highest-delivering segments first
context_conditions: Effectiveness proportional to hillslope soil infiltration rate; greater response in basins with higher infiltration capacity; post-wildfire reduced infiltration diminishes disconnection benefit
evidence_quote: With addition of the 9,762 engineered drains, these proportions dropped to 4%–29% (average 14%)
locator: Results: Effectiveness of Existing Road Surfacing and Engineered Drainage Structures; Tables 5–6

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % reduction in road surface erodibility from gravel/rock surfacing; reductions in sediment production ranged 0.5–7.8% across basins
design_spec_detail: Gravel/rock surfacing assumed to produce 80% reduction in erodibility (Swift 1984; Coe 2006; Barrett et al. 2012); proportion of roads rocked ranged 2–12%
context_conditions: Only reduces sediment delivery when applied to segments already delivering to streams; rocking alone has limited basin-scale impact unless combined with optimised drain placement
evidence_quote: rocking reduces sediment production, it will only reduce sediment delivery when applied to segments that deliver sediment to streams
locator: Results: Optimizing Placement of New Drains and Rock Surfacing; Table 4; Table 6

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % of total possible sediment reduction achieved by first 10% of optimally placed drains (Rock Creek example)
design_spec_detail: Optimal new drain locations identified by READI priority-queue algorithm at 1-m increments; minimum drain spacing 30 m; 0.4–2.0 new drains/km needed to reach minimum achievable delivery
context_conditions: Diminishing returns with each additional drain; best locations where roads parallel streams or approach crossings; less effective post-wildfire due to reduced soil infiltration
evidence_quote: 50% of total possible sediment reduction is achieved in the first 20 drains (10% of total drains)
locator: Results: Optimizing Placement of New Drains and Rock Surfacing; Figure 5; Table 6

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: BMPs associated with reduced erosion frequency in PCA; negative weighting of BMP variables with erosion frequency

context_conditions: Effect masked by road grade and slope position variables; most influential on steep roads
evidence_quote: the application of design interventions used to slow the flow of water...have proven effective in minimizing erosion on unpaved roads

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: presence of BMPs reduced erosion frequency in field survey statistical analysis
design_spec_detail: not reported
context_conditions: Rural unpaved municipal roads, northeastern USA; steep gradient roads benefit most
evidence_quote: The presence of BMPs effectively reduced erosion frequency.

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: Stone-lined ditches required on roads with grade >=5% per Vermont Better Backroads guidelines (VBB 2009); non-compliance measured as proportion of steep road without stone-lined ditch
context_conditions: Roads with grade >=5%; state municipal road management guidelines
evidence_quote: statewide municipal road management guidelines call for different management practices on roads with grades greater than or equal to 5%

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported

context_conditions: Recorded on 52 surveyed road segments; turnouts were most frequently applied BMP (424 of 609 total BMPs, 70%)
evidence_quote: the most frequently recorded management practice was turnouts (70%), which were recorded in 424 independent locations

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: not reported
design_spec_detail: not reported

evidence_quote: The second most frequently applied management practice was stone-lined ditches (11%).

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: targeting BMPs in hot-spot areas predicted to yield meaningful water quality reductions

evidence_quote: using BMPs in 'hot spot' areas may provide tangible, meaningful reductions in water quality impairments

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % mean structural SC decrease (ΔAICN-OUTS) in sub-catchments with >100 m ha-1 barrier density
design_spec_detail: Log erosion barriers: max 15 m length, ~10 m spacing between barriers, staggered pattern, max height 25 cm (40 cm near trails); branches stacked behind logs as energy dissipater; fixed with stakes or stumps
context_conditions: Effective only at density >100 m ha-1; low-density sub-catchments (<100 m ha-1) showed no significant difference from untreated; limited by lack of woody material on south-facing slopes
evidence_quote: sub-catchments with a higher density of built barriers (>100 m ha-1) had the lowest increment with ΔAICN-OUTS = -0.879%
locator: Results Section 3.3; Methods Section 2.1; Discussion Section 4.3.1

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: % mean structural SC decrease (ΔAICN-OUTS) for mechanically subsoiled afforestation areas vs -1.44% for untreated
design_spec_detail: Afforestation using shrub species (Arbutus unedo, Rhamnus lycioides, Nerium oleander, Salvia rosmarinus, Olea europaea var sylvestris, Phyllirea angustifolia, Viburnum tinus); two soil preparation methods: mechanical subsoiling and manual digging; implemented in C. Pin catchment
context_conditions: Mechanical subsoiling (SS) significantly reduced SC vs untreated and manual digging; manual digging (D) showed no significant difference from untreated; both methods increase functional SC under high rainfall erosivity
evidence_quote: SS areas had the greatest mean decrease with ΔAICN-OUTS = -3.06%... D-areas showed values of ΔAICN-OUTS = -7.94%

effectiveness_unit_or_basis: Check-dam SSY ranged 0.81-1.96 Mg ha-1 yr-1 in sub-catchments with upstream measures vs higher SSY where measures absent; positive correlation R2=0.752 between ΔAICN-OUTS and SSY
design_spec_detail: Concrete check-dams: height 3-6.5 m, width 21-39 m, built on principal channels close to main forest roads. Rock check-dams: max height 2 m on secondary tributary channels, minimum distance between dams depends on RC height and channel slope (minimum 2 m), materials: rocks and concrete
context_conditions: Concrete check-dam effect on SC index not detectable at 2 m DEM resolution; rock check-dams produced no significant SC change detectable by model; sub-catchments with higher measure density upstream showed lower SSY
evidence_quote: The expected disconnectivity of upstream areas produced by RC and CC on the SC maps was not noticeable at the AICN-OUT maps
locator: Results Section 3.4; Methods Section 2.1; Discussion Section 4.4
